title: docs(data-modeling): name what the lookup dependsOn formula check does not see on import
body:
Part of #37936

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 用户能看到什么变化：导入数据的人在文档的导入映射页上读到，作者时的检查在哪几种情况下看不到问题，导入时仍会遇到“无法在范围内查找”的提示；产品行为不变。
- 为什么做：这是上一轮查找字段依赖筛选收严之后，复审留下的文档尾巴，原句把检查说得比实际更全。
- 出错会怎样：只改一段文档，读者最多读到不准确的说明，可以直接撤回。
- 要你做的：无（另一半，树形字段是否也该受检查，等席位转决策）。

## What changes

`content/docs/data-modeling/import-mappings.mdx`, one paragraph. The sentence "so an import meets this sentence only on metadata stored before that check" overstated the authoring check that refuses a `dependsOn` filter key naming a formula of the target. It now says the check judges a `lookup`, `master_detail` or `user` field against the objects it can see, and names the cases where an import still meets the could-not-be-looked-up sentence. Each case was measured against `origin/main` at 6e06729a9 before it was named:

1. **Metadata stored before the check** (unchanged from the old sentence).
2. **A `tree` field, or a legacy `reference` field.** The lint resolves the referenced half only on `PICKER_FIELD_TYPES = lookup, master_detail, user` (`packages/lint/src/validate-object-field-refs.ts:442`, applied at `:1002`); the importer scopes by `dependsOn` on every type in `IMPORT_REFERENCE_TYPES` (`packages/spec/src/data/field-value.zod.ts:154-155` adds `tree`, `packages/spec/src/data/import-coercion.ts:44-47` adds `reference`; read at `packages/core/src/utils/import-coerce.ts:1056-1061`). Probe: the same task/project pair with the target field a formula gives one `computed on read` finding for `lookup` and `master_detail`, zero for `tree` and `reference`.
3. **`os validate` of a stack that does not hold both objects.** The rule's graph is the validated stack alone (`indexServedObjectGraph(stack)`, `validate-object-field-refs.ts:683`), the formula check reads `graph.get(against)?.fields` (`:1054`), and only the stack's own objects are walked (`:998`). Probe: a lookup whose target is not in the stack gives zero findings; the control with the formula target in the stack gives one. The same holds for the owning side: a target field turned into a formula in a package validated without the owning object is never judged there.

The card's third wording, "a target field changed from stored to formula after the owning object was published", was **measured false for the runtime publish gate** and is not named as a gap there. The gate's context is every object the environment serves, registry plus stored rows (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-authoring-gate.ts:527-552`); its differential drops the written item from the baseline (`packages/lint/src/runtime-gate.ts:968`) and charges findings the candidate adds (`addedFindings`, `:1344`). Probe: writing the target object with the field now a formula, while the owning object sits in the context, is refused with `objects.pr_task.fields.project.dependsOn[0].param "acct_label" is a formula field of "pr_project", computed on read`. The page says so in its last sentence. The case survives only on the CLI, as part of item 3.

## Tests

Docs-only. No test changed. The measurements above came from a throwaway vitest file in `packages/lint/src` (deleted before commit, never pushed), run as `pnpm --filter @objectstack/lint exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 PROBE_FILE` after building the lint dependency closure; it printed:

<details><summary>probe output (4 tests passed)</summary>

```text
C ["objects[0].fields.project.dependsOn[0].param"]
CASE1 []
CASE3-tree []
CASE3-reference []
CASE3-master_detail ["objects[0].fields.project.dependsOn[0].param"]
CASE2-gate-target-write: includes objects.pr_task.fields.project.dependsOn[0].param ... computed on read
CASE2-control-owner-write ["objects.pr_task.fields.project.dependsOn[0].param"]
CASE1-gate-owner-write-target-absent []
```

</details>

## Acceptance notes

**N2 is measured here, not changed** (the card stays open). Readings, each against `origin/main` at 6e06729a9:

- (a) **The spec.** `dependsOn`'s describe (`packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts:2657`) declares candidate-query scoping "For `lookup`/`master_detail`" and option gating for `select`/`multiselect`/`radio`; it names neither `tree` nor `user` nor `reference`. The Studio field form offers `dependsOn` only on `lookup`, `master_detail`, `select`, `multiselect`, `radio`, `checkboxes` (`packages/spec/src/data/field.metadata-form.ts:327`). Control: the schema itself does not gate `dependsOn` by type (`field.zod.ts:2650`), so a `tree` field carrying it parses.
- (b) **The importer.** Scopes by `dependsOn` on `lookup`, `master_detail`, `user`, `tree` (`REFERENCE_VALUE_TYPES`, `field-value.zod.ts:154-155`) and `reference` (`import-coercion.ts:44-47`), read at `import-coerce.ts:1056-1061`. A `tree` with no `reference` is not scoped (`:1056`, `!meta?.reference`).
- (c) **The lint.** Judges the referenced half of `dependsOn` only on `lookup`, `master_detail`, `user` (`validate-object-field-refs.ts:442`, `:1002`). Its docblock says on any other type "those keys have no reader" (`:436-441`). Counter-reading: the console renders `tree` with the lookup widget (`ui/packages/fields/src/field-type-alias.ts:142`, `tree: 'field:lookup'`), the widget that reads `dependsOn`. And a `tree` field's `reference` may only name its own object (`packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts:2018`), so its target is always in the stack the lint sees.
- (d) **Producers.** `git grep` over `examples/`, `packages/platform-objects/`, `skills/`: `tree` fields at 3 source sites (`examples/app-showcase/src/data/objects/field-zoo.object.ts:122`, `examples/app-showcase/src/ui/views/business-unit.view.ts:27`, `packages/platform-objects/src/identity/sys-business-unit.object.ts:55`) plus one skill sample (`skills/objectstack-data/rules/relationships.md:147`); `type: 'reference'` at 0 sites. None of them carries `dependsOn`: zero files hold both outside a `CHANGELOG.md` and the skill page, whose `dependsOn` mention is the lookup paragraph at `:106`, not the tree sample. Control: the same grep finds `dependsOn` in 3 example object files (`cascading-select`, `contact`, `invoice`), all on lookup or option fields. Sibling repos (hotcrm, cloud) were not measured.

The two options the card names, for the seat:

- **A. The lint covers the importer's set** (add `tree` and `reference` to the types whose `dependsOn` reference half is judged). Cost: a narrowing of `@objectstack/lint` (Clause-② narrowing, minor), zero known producers broken by (d). It matches the console, which already reads `dependsOn` on `tree`. `reference` is not a `FieldType` the parse accepts, so it only matters for legacy stored rows the lint sees. Size XS.
- **B. The importer stops scoping types the spec does not declare it for** (scope only on `lookup`/`master_detail`, maybe `user`). Cost: an import behaviour change in `@objectstack/core`. A `tree` cell that is scoped today would resolve across the whole object, and the import would disagree with the console picker, which still filters a `tree` by `dependsOn`. Also needs a spec describe decision on `user`. Size S.

Recommendation: A. It closes the lint gap without opening a new one between the import and the picker. The spec describe would then name `tree` beside `lookup`/`master_detail` (prose that follows the ruling).

## Verification

Two-minute check: open `content/docs/data-modeling/import-mappings.mdx` at the paragraph beginning "A `dependsOn` entry whose `param` names a target field". It should list three cases (stored metadata, `tree`/legacy `reference`, an `os validate` of a stack without both objects) and end saying the runtime publish gate refuses turning such a target field into a formula.

Read first: the one changed paragraph, lines 372-386.
